mechanism_narrative: A higher unemployment rate (UNRATE) indicates a weakening labor market and reduced consumer spending, which typically leads to lower corporate earnings and negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 55% of observations when UNRATE is above its 50th percentile, or the Rank IC over a 3-year rolling window is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A housing starts level (HOUST) above 1300 thousand units signals strong residential construction activity, indicating a robust economy and positive consumer sentiment, which drives positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 55% of triggered instances (HOUST > 1300), or the Rank IC over a 3-year rolling window is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: The product of the inflation rate (CPIAUCSL) and the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) captures the real interest rate pressure on equity valuations; a higher product value indicates a more restrictive monetary environment, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: The Rank IC for the product of CPIAUCSL and FEDFUNDS over a 3-year rolling window is below 0.03, or the product has a positive correlation with 20-day SPX returns in more than 55% of observations.

mechanism_narrative: In a monetary tightening cycle (FEDFUNDS > 4.5%), a higher unemployment rate (UNRATE) signals that the economy is slowing and the Federal Reserve may soon cut rates, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 55% of instances when FEDFUNDS > 4.5% and UNRATE is above 4.3%, or the Rank IC for the signal is below 0.03 over a 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A higher industrial production level (INDPRO) indicates robust manufacturing and economic activity, which supports corporate profits and drives positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are negative in more than 55% of observations when INDPRO is above its 50th percentile, or the Rank IC over a 3-year rolling window is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) above 4.5% signals an ongoing monetary tightening cycle, which increases borrowing costs and reduces corporate investment, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are positive in more than 55% of triggered instances (FEDFUNDS > 4.5%), or the Rank IC over a 3-year rolling window is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A higher retail sales level (RSAFS) indicates strong consumer spending, which boosts corporate revenues and drives positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are negative in more than 55% of observations when RSAFS is above its 50th percentile, or the Rank IC over a 3-year rolling window is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: An unemployment rate (UNRATE) below 4.0% signals an overheating labor market and potential inflation, prompting the Federal Reserve to tighten monetary policy, which leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are positive in more than 55% of triggered instances (UNRATE < 4.0), or the Rank IC over a 3-year rolling window is below 0.03.
